answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it can post jobs or earn reputation. The protocol caps how much influence one locked token grants, so splitting a stake across many accounts does not multiply voting power. A sable account that behaves honestly can recover its deposit after the lock, but proven fraud triggers slashing, making a Sybil campaign costly in capital and time. The attacker must also keep funds immobilized while honest agents exchange nectar and update trust scores as new evidence causes delta changes.
